Search breadth: very thorough.

You are scouting the Fortress language repository at /home/user/fortress (Sun/Oracle's Fortress, 2003-2012, being revived; toolchain in Java+Scala under ProjectFortress/, stdlib in Fortress under Library/). Your mission: produce a CONCISE BUT PRECISE module map of the territory, suitable as a committed guide for developers new to the repo — verifying, correcting, and completing the draft map below.

DRAFT MAP TO VERIFY (written earlier from partial exploration; treat every count and claim as unverified):

- Pipeline for a .fss file, packages under ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/:
  1. Parsing: grammar in .rats files (Rats!/xtc packrat generator), generated parsers in parser/ (claimed 5 huge files); parser_util/ (claimed 89 files) hand-written support (unicode operator precedence, layout); syntax_abstractions/ (claimed 30 files) = extensible-syntax machinery.
  2. AST: nodes/ (claimed 1,071 ASTGen-generated files) + nodes_util/ (hand-written factories/utilities); source of truth astgen/Fortress.ast; claim: Library/FortressAst.fss is a generated Fortress-level mirror of the AST.
  3. Static analysis: compiler/ (claimed 197 Java files: Disambiguator, Desugarer, StaticChecker, indexing) + scala_src/ (claimed 59 Scala files: the type checker proper — typechecker, overloading, types, disambiguator subpackages). Claim: original type checker was Java, rewritten in Scala ~2009-2011.
  4a. Interpreter path: interpreter/ (claimed 246 files), tree-walking evaluator, reference semantics.
  4b. Compiler path: compiler/codegen (ASM bytecode emission), compiler/asmbytecodeoptimizer, runtimeSystem/ (claimed 25 files) work-stealing runtime the emitted code links against.
  - Support: repository/ (component cache), nativeHelpers/ (FFI shims), useful/ (claimed 131-file utility grab-bag), unicode/ (operator table generation), linker/, ant_tasks/, astgen/ (extensions to ASTGen).
- Stdlib: Library/ at repo root, claimed 53 components (.fss + .fsi pairs), FortressLibrary.fss claimed 4,518-line core prelude; compiler path uses a parallel smaller chain (CompilerBuiltin, CompilerLibrary, CompilerAlgebra).

YOUR TASKS:
1. Enumerate ALL packages under ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/ (ls the directory) with accurate file counts (count .java and .scala separately where mixed). Flag any package the draft omits entirely (e.g. exceptions/, env-related, tests/, tools/?) and say in one line what each omitted one does (open a representative file or two).
2. Verify or correct every count and factual claim in the draft (parser file count, nodes count, scala_src breakdown, interpreter count, Library component count, FortressLibrary.fss line count, .fss/.fsi pairing). For the FortressAst.fss claim, check whether it is actually generated from Fortress.ast (look for generator code in astgen/ or build.xml targets, or a generated-file header in FortressAst.fss).
3. Check the Scala-rewrite history claim cheaply: git log --follow --format='%ad %s' --date=short on a couple of scala_src typechecker files (first commit dates), or git log --diff-filter=A on the scala_src dir. One or two commands, don't go deep.
4. Enumerate top-level repo directories (ls /home/user/fortress) and classify each in one line: live toolchain / stdlib / spec-and-papers / historical artifact / revival-era / build byproduct. Note any that are dead weight or surprising.
5. Identify the 3-5 entry points a new developer actually touches: the Shell main class, bin/fortress script chain, build.xml key targets, where tests live (ProjectFortress/tests? compiler_tests? other_compiler_tests? static_tests?) — with one line each on what they are, verified by looking.
6. Note anything load-bearing the draft misses that a "curious dev" guide should mention (e.g. Fortress.ast size, the .rats file locations and count, StandardLibrary vs built-ins wiring, environment/ or env classes, the Fortify LaTeX renderer's role).

Do NOT propose prose for the README — return raw verified facts as a structured report: corrected map, per-package one-liners with counts, corrections list (draft said X, actually Y), omissions list, entry points, top-level classification. Precision over volume; every number you report must come from a command you ran, and mark anything you could not verify as UNVERIFIED.

# Fortress

Fortress was Sun Microsystems' experimental programming language for
high-performance computation, designed at Sun Labs under **Guy L. Steele Jr.**
and developed from 2003 to 2012. Its ambition was captured in its motto: *"to
do for Fortran what Java did for C."* In practice it became something broader —
a laboratory for programming-language ideas that are still being absorbed by
mainstream languages today:

- **A growable language.** Following Steele's "Growing a Language" (OOPSLA
  1998), almost everything — operators, loops, even the parallel machinery of
  `∑` and friends — is defined in libraries, not the compiler.
- **A mathematical language.** Syntax modeled on whiteboard mathematics:
  Unicode operators (`∈`, `⊆`, `⌊x⌋`, `∑`), juxtaposition as a user-definable
  operator (`3 sin pi x`), nontransitive operator precedence (`a+b ∨ c+d` is
  rejected rather than misparsed), and comments that render as wiki markup.
- **A parallel language.** Loops, tuples, argument evaluation, and big
  reduction operators are implicitly parallel; a work-stealing runtime
  balances the load ("do for processors what GC does for memory"); `atomic`
  blocks are backed by transactional memory.
- **Traits, multiple inheritance, and symmetric multimethod dispatch**, with
  overloading checked by the Meet Rule — plus algebraic traits (`Monoid`,
  `Ring`, …) and design-by-contract woven into the type system.

This repository is a **revival** of that codebase: the complete surviving
history (5,397 commits, January 2007 – August 2012) carried forward to a
modern toolchain, with a fully green test suite — the first in this lineage.

- Builds and runs on **JDK 25** with Scala 2.13.18 and ASM 9 (JDK 8–21 also

## 6. Load-bearing things the draft misses

- **`compiler/WellKnownNames.java` is the built-ins/stdlib switch.** It holds the mutable globals `_fortressLibrary`, `_fortressBuiltin`, `_anyTypeLibrary`, `_compilerAlgebra`, `_defaultLibrary[]`, plus `anyTypeName="Any"`, `objectTypeName="Object"`, `defaultSelfName="self"`, `secretSelfName="$self"`. Methods `useCompilerLibraries()` (line 113) and `useFortressLibraries()` (line 128) flip the whole toolchain between the two library chains at runtime — `useCompilerLibraries()` rebinds `_fortressBuiltin = "CompilerBuiltin"` and swaps `_defaultLibrary`. `areCompilerLibraries()` queries it. This one file is how the interpreter path and compiler path get different preludes.
- **Four parsers, not one.** `Fortress.rats` (main), `preparser/PreFortress.rats` (pre-parse pass for imports/grammar discovery), `templateparser/TemplateParser.rats` (syntax-abstraction templates), `import_collector/ImportCollector.rats`. `syntax_abstractions/` exists to generate new parsers at compile time from user grammars.
- **Two separate environment subsystems**, easy to conflate: `interpreter/env/` (15 files, runtime environments for the evaluator) vs `compiler/environments/` (6 files, `TopLevelEnvGen`-style compiled environment classes) vs `scala_src/typechecker/staticenv/` (static type environments). Plus `compiler/disambiguator/TopLevelEnv.java`.
- **`repository/ProjectProperties.java`** — resolves `FORTRESS_HOME`/`BASEDIR`; every test harness and cache path goes through it. First stop when paths misbehave.
- **`compiler/NamingCzar.java` + `runtimeSystem/Naming.java`** — the Fortress-name-to-JVM-name mangling scheme, shared between codegen and the runtime's `Instantiater` (which materializes generic instantiations at class-load time). Non-obvious and central to the compiler path.
- **`tools/FortressAstToConcrete.java`** — AST-to-source unparser backing `fortress unparse`; useful for debugging desugaring.
- **`useful/` is not purely a grab-bag** — it is dominated by hand-rolled persistent balanced-tree collections (`BATree`, `BASet`, `BATreeEC`, `ABoundingMap`), with JUnit tests interleaved in the same package.
- **`Fortify`** renders Fortress source as typeset LaTeX math; it is why the spec and papers can quote real library code. Wired via `bin/fortify`, `ant_tasks/FortifyTask.java`, and `ant specification`.
- **Generated-but-committed** (repeated because it bites): `nodes/`, `parser/*.java`, `scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`, `Library/FortressAst.fss|.fsi` are all in git and all regenerable. `ant makeAST` also post-processes with a `<replace>` rewriting `java.lang.Object` → `Object` across `nodes/`.
